newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks close mixed in busy trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks close mixed in busy trade.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Thursday with drugs concern Pliva dominating trade and market participants foresaw busy trade continuing in the next weeks.
"We are in a positive cycle now and I think this should be felt in the weeks ahead," Davor Relja of Faktor brokerage told Reuters.
Eight of 18 active issue rose on Thursday, eight fell and two were flat. Volume rose to 20,234 units from 19,690 and turnover fell to 9.6 million kuna from 10.3 million.

Blue chip Pliva pharmaceutical was the most active stock, accounting for one third of the total trade with 7,828 shares sold. It closed four kuna lower at 495 after trading mixed in 484-501 kuna range.
Its global depository receipts (GDR's) in London rose to $16.69 from Wednesday's close at $16.55.
Traders partly ascribed Pliva's recovery to a worldwide bullish trend in pharmaceuticals but said the stock had reached its current maximum and would not grow further.
Five of six active hoteliers posted new gains on Thursday, but market analysts said they were lifted by the general surge of the market and significant growth was not due before autumn.
"Plava Laguna, where foreign investors have a considerable stake, may be the only exception," Relja said.
Laguna added five kuna to 1,505 on volume of 447 shares.

Another market heavyweight Zagrebacka Banka was among the losers, sliding 20 kuna to 1,960 with 1,023 shares changing hands. Traders said the stock was likely to rise soon and end the period of stagnation.

Thursday's biggest gainer was electrical concern Koncar which added 260 kuna or 27.7 percent to 1,200 on a meagre volume of 80. The company signed a contract with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell on Tuesday to help float some 30 percent of its capital on the international market.
Liquor producer Badel, which last traded in February, led the decliners. It lost 30 kuna to a 100 on volume of 91.
Food company Podravka which won a 20 million German marks loan from Bank Austria on Tuesday, lost two kuna to 271 kuna on volme of 3,216.

"Not much will change here before there is some foreign investment or a similar sort of good news, and the same goes for (chocolate maker) Kras," said Relja. Kras lost six kuna to 434 on modest volume of 309 shares.
